aspects.says: Arrays.parallelSetAll, parallelPrefix and parallelSort already run plain array work on fork/join.
aspects.reason: a test sees only the resulting array, so it cannot tell a built-in from a hand-written action; the page names them as a choice, not a skill

aspects.says: Leaves that add to one shared total count locally and add to it once per leaf, rather than once per element.
basis: section:Leaves Count Locally and Add to the Shared Total Once

aspects.says: Subtasks of an in-place action write disjoint ranges; an inclusive midpoint changes the boundary elements twice, the same ones every run.
basis: section:Subtasks Write Disjoint Ranges and Read Nothing Another Subtask Writes

aspects.says: When a leaf throws, invoke() rethrows but every leaf that ran keeps its writes, so the array is left partly changed.
basis: section:A Failure Leaves the Array Partly Changed, So Write to a Copy

aspects.says: invokeAll(left, right) forks one task, runs the other on the current thread and waits for the first, so the two halves run at once and a task can also do work after its subtasks are done.
basis: section:A RecursiveAction Is Finished Only When compute() Has Waited for Its Subtasks

aspects.says: A leaf that reads elements of another leaf's range while that leaf rewrites them gives a result that depends on the schedule; reading one array and writing another removes it.
basis: section:Subtasks Write Disjoint Ranges and Read Nothing Another Subtask Writes

aspects.says: When an action's whole output is one number, a RecursiveTask returns it without shared state.
basis: section:Leaves Count Locally and Add to the Shared Total Once
aspects.reason: which task type a solution picks is invisible to a test; unit 6.6.1.2 practises RecursiveTask

aspects.says: A plain shared field updated by several leaves loses updates silently, even when each leaf adds only once.
basis: section:Leaves Count Locally and Add to the Shared Total Once

aspects.says: invokeAll rethrows a failure without waiting for a subtask already running, which keeps writing after the caller has caught the exception, so a rollback in the catch can be overwritten.
basis: section:A Failure Leaves the Array Partly Changed, So Write to a Copy

aspects.says: A RecursiveAction's compute() must wait for its subtasks, as invokeAll does; forking them and returning lets invoke() return while the leaves are still writing.
basis: section:A RecursiveAction Is Finished Only When compute() Has Waited for Its Subtasks

aspects.says: Running the action on a copy and publishing it only when invoke() returns normally leaves the original untouched on failure.
basis: section:A Failure Leaves the Array Partly Changed, So Write to a Copy
